findings.title: Pause action is never rendered in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: The menu only renders MenuItemPauseRule when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true. In the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem/GrafanaGroupLoader/FilterView) no rulerRule is passed, so rulerRule is undefined and the condition is always false, even though the PR computes grafanaPauseAbility from promRule at lines 67-83. Users in the alert list can therefore never pause/unpause a Grafana rule from this menu.

findings.title: Delete action is never rendered in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined by design (ruler requests were removed), so despite grafanaDeleteAbility being computed from promRule at lines 67-87, Delete never appears. This is confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, which grants AlertingRuleDelete and expects only 4 menu items with no Delete. Users cannot delete Grafana rules from the list view menu.

findings.title: Silence drawer cannot open in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: handleSilence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer=true, but the drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true and it requires `rulerRule={rule}`. In the list view RuleActionsButtons is now called with only promRule (see GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx line 47), so rule is undefined, the condition is false, and clicking 'Silence notifications' (which the new Grafana abilities can enable) does nothing.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to block Update/Delete/Pause/Duplicate for federated (Mimir cross-tenant) groups. The refactor hard-codes `const isFederated = false` with only a TODO. CombinedRule consumers will now report federated rules as supported for edit/delete/pause (subject only to isEditable/isRemovable), allowing actions the backend/UI previously forbade for federated groups.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered list is rendered without a React key
findings.body: The 'grafana' branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem> without `key={key}`, unlike the 'datasource' branch on line 165 and the Unknown branch on line 168 which both pass key. FilterView builds a deduplicated artificial key via getRuleKey for exactly this purpose. Without it React warns and, more importantly, may reuse component instances (including RuleActionsButtons state such as silence drawer/delete modal/redirect state) for different rules when the infinite-scroll list appends or reorders, showing actions for the wrong rule.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules lose Pause/Restore abilities in list view
findings.body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates Pause and Restore (and ModifyExport/DeletePermanently) on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for recording rules. The ruler-based implementation gated Pause on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes Grafana recording rules, and GrafanaPromRuleDTO carries isPaused for both types. In the ruler-free list view a recording rule can therefore no longer be paused/resumed (and AlertRuleMenu's pause item would be disabled even if it were rendered).

findings.title: Rule link loses the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail returned to the list with its filters. The new component builds the href with no query params, so the detail view loses the return-to-list context the old list item preserved.
